significance: James I's Witchcraft Act (1 Jac. I c. 12) replaced the 1563 Elizabethan statute with stricter provisions, making first-offence maleficium capital, expanding prosecutable acts, and reflecting the new king's personal demonological engagement documented in his Daemonologie (1597). The Act remained in force until 1736.
source_method: Statutes of the Realm, 1 Jac. I c. 12; analyzed in Levack, The Witch-Hunt in Early Modern Europe (2006); Hutton, The Witch (2017)
